Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 61, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Saff (The Ranks), because the word al-saff (ṣaff) occurs in it. It refers to the fighting of the believers in the cause of Allah, standing like a firm, tightly joined structure (bunyan maḥkam mutaraṣṣ), through which the enemy cannot penetrate.

Some of the Surah's Aims

• Encouraging jihad (striving in the cause of Allah, i.e., struggle in His path) and steadfastness in it; promising sincere faith and jihad a good reward and victory; and calling the believers to support the religion and to follow the example of the truthful, such as the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn) of ʿIsā, the companions of ʿIsā, when he called them to support Allah, and they responded.

• Warning against harming the Messenger (ﷺ), and giving the example of the conduct of the Jews toward Mūsā and ʿĪsā (peace be upon them both), as consolation to the Messenger (ﷺ); and pointing to the sunnah (established way) of Allah in granting victory to His religion, His prophets and His allies; and explaining the position of the enemies of the religion by a parable of their determination to fight the religion of Allah: like one who wants to extinguish the light of the sun with his mouth.

[Tafsir]

Everything in the heavens and everything on the earth glorifies Allah, exalting Him above everything unfitting for Him, and He is al-ʿAzīz (the Mighty), who cannot be overcome, al-Ḥakīm (the Wise) in His sayings and His actions.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, why do you promise what you do not do, or say what you do not fulfill? This is a rebuke against one whose action contradicts his words.
"It is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do."

Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, as though they were a solid structure, firmly joined, that the enemy cannot penetrate. This verse shows the excellence of jihad and of those who strive in it, for Allah, glory be to Him, loves His believing servants when they stand in rows facing the enemies of Allah, fighting them in His cause.

Mention to your people, O Messenger, when Moses, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him), said to his people: "Why do you harm me with words and deeds, when you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?" So when they deviated from the truth, despite knowing it, and persisted in that, Allah turned their hearts away from accepting guidance, as a punishment for their deviation which they had chosen for themselves. And Allah does not guide the people who transgress obedience and the path of truth.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 61, verse 6:

Remember, O Messenger, for your people, when Jesus, son of Mary, said to his people: "Indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and giving good news of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is 'Ahmad,' and he is Muhammad (ﷺ), and calling to belief in him. So when Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them with the clear signs, they said: 'This that you have brought is clear magic.'"

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 61, verse 7:

There is no one more unjust and more transgressive than the one who fabricates lies against God and sets up partners with Him in worship, while he is being invited to enter Islam and to devote worship to God alone. God does not guide to what is good for them those who wrong themselves through disbelief and polytheism.

Those wrongdoers want to extinguish the truth with which Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, which is the Qur'an, by means of their false words. But God will make His truth prevail by perfecting His religion, even if the deniers and rejecters dislike it.

Allah is the One who sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with the Qur'an and the religion of Islam, so that He might make it prevail over all other religions that oppose it, even though the polytheists dislike that.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 61, verse 10:**

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law, shall I guide you to a trade of great worth that will save you from a painful punishment?

You continue in your faith in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah, to support His religion with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you than worldly trade, if you know the harms and benefits of things, so comply with that.

If you (believers) do what Allah has commanded you, He will cover over your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and into pleasant, pure dwellings in gardens of everlasting residence that never end. That is the great success, with no success beyond it. And there is another blessing you love, believers: victory from Allah coming to you, and a near conquest accomplished at your hands. So give good tidings to the believers, O Prophet, of victory and conquest in this world, and of Paradise in the Hereafter.

If you (believers) do what Allah has commanded you, He will cover over your sins and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and into pleasant, pure dwellings in gardens of everlasting residence that never end. That is the great success, with no success beyond it. And there is another blessing you love, believers: victory from Allah coming to you, and a near conquest accomplished at your hands. So give good tidings to the believers, O Prophet, of victory and conquest in this world, and of Paradise in the Hereafter.

O you who have believed, be supporters of Allah's religion, as the chosen disciples of Jesus and his sincere companions were supporters of Allah's religion when Jesus said to them: "Who will be my helpers in Allah's cause?" (﴿Who are my helpers for Allah?﴾). They said: "We are the supporters of Allah's religion." Then a group of the Children of Israel believed, and a group disbelieved. So We strengthened those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, and We aided them against those who opposed them from the sects of the Christians, and they became dominant over them; and that was by the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ).
